title: A Choir for the Smile
premise: Ivo Blackwood takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Primary, where a class photo from 1974 shows eleven children and the school records list only ten. As frost patterns bloom indoors spelling names, and her grandmother's photographs sprout an extra chair that creeps closer each day, Ivo realizes the missing child, Elowen, was never lost — she was given, traded by the village to something beneath the frost for another hard winter. The choir the school still sings each December is not a carol but an invitation, renewed annually by a teacher's signature. To end it, Ivo must return what was taken: her grandmother's confession, hidden in the hymnal's spine, and finally her own name offered in Elowen's place — until love, in the form of her grandmother's dying apology sung back through the frost, breaks the bargain instead.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou is a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in villages where winter was treated as a creditor. She writes horror about institutions that mistake tradition for innocence.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Desk
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Arriving at Hollowmere, Ivo counts ten pupils but finds an eleventh desk, warm. The headmaster, Mr. Pell, laughs it off as old furniture. That night she hears humming through the heating pipes. Emotional beat: unease dressed as professional optimism.

chapters.title: Class Photograph, 1974
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the archive she finds the 1974 photo: eleven smiling children, one face scratched out. Records list ten. A retired secretary warns her never to lead the December choir. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Grandma Keeps in the Hallway
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, visiting grandmother Maren. Old family photos now include an extra chair, closer in each print, and Maren refuses to look at them. Frost ferns bloom on the inside of the windows though it isn't cold. Emotional beat: love shadowed by a shared secret.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Pell insists she take over choir practice for the Winter Service. The children sing a melody none of them were taught, perfectly, eyes forward. One girl, Sef, whispers that 'the quiet one' likes it when they harmonize. Emotional beat: complicity beginning.

chapters.title: The Chair at the Table
chapters.summary: POV Maren (interleaved with Ivo). Maren's memory slips between 1974 and now; the chair arrives at her kitchen table, and someone small sits in it. She begins writing a confession she cannot finish. Emotional beat: guilt as haunting.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A pupil stops coming to school; his family says he 'joined the choir.' The register corrects itself overnight, erasing him. Pell's signature appears on documents Ivo never signed. Emotional beat: horror of bureaucratic erasure.

chapters.title: Hymnal
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Splitting the school hymnal's spine, she finds Maren's 1974 confession: the village gave Elowen Vane to the frost-thing after a starving winter, and every teacher since has renewed the debt by conducting the choir. Emotional beat: betrayal of everything she trusted.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boiler
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Beneath the school, past the boiler, she finds the cold room where the frost keeps its pattern — and Elowen, unchanged, singing. Pell blocks the stairs: the bargain is the town's warmth, its life. Take it up with the frost, he says. Emotional beat: power's banality.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. On the night of the Winter Service, Ivo leads the choir but changes the words to Maren's finished confession — an apology, a naming, a returning. The frost writes Elowen's name across every window, then unwrites it. The thing rises to claim the singer. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ten Chairs
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, epilogue. Spring. Ten desks, ten chairs, no extra anywhere; Sef remembers a friend she can't name and cries without knowing why. Maren dies peacefully, forgiven. In the last photograph Ivo takes, everyone smiles — and this time, counting twice, no one is extra. Emotional beat: grief braided with release.
